title: Offline Makes Online Better: Calibrated Cache Compression for Video Generation
summary: CALM replaces uniform-ratio token merging in KV-cache compression for autoregressive video generation with a fixed layer-head merging allocation, selected offline via an attention-output error proxy and applied at inference through dynamic programming under a given cache budget. The cost is a one-time offline calibration per model, plus dependence on the assumption that attention-output error predicts end-to-end video quality; inference overhead itself is minimal once the risk map is built. It can fail if the calibrated sensitivity map does not transfer to new prompts, model versions, or cache budgets far from those used in calibration, and the 21% LPIPS gain is reported against the method's own uniform-merging baseline, not against uncompressed generation.
rationale: It is directly deployable on a single-GPU inference setup and reduces KV-cache memory with a measurable quality gain, but the benefit must be validated on the reader's specific video model, prompts, and memory budget before production adoption.

The cost is a one-time offline calibration per model, plus dependence on the assumption that attention-output error predicts end-to-end video quality; inference overhead itself is minimal once the risk map is built. It can fail if the calibrated sensitivity map does not transfer to new prompts, model versions, or cache budgets far from those used in calibration, and the 21% LPIPS gain is reported against the method's own uniform-merging baseline, not against uncompressed generation.
Reduces LPIPS to original videos by around 21% relative to uniform token merging at the same memory budget, with higher video-quality scores, across three autoregressive video models.
